key_insight: The paper extends the J-integral to 3D quasicontinuum fracture simulations and adds uncertainty quantification so crack-driving force estimates can be trusted across atomistic-to-continuum scales.
engineering_relevance: This gives fracture engineers a practical way to compute energy release rates in multiscale models, supporting larger simulations while still resolving crack-tip atomistic effects.
method: Implemented J-integral in QC3D under plane strain using Cauchy-Born-derived continuum fields.
Validated against LEFM and virtual crack extension across linear elasticity, nonlinear Cauchy-Born without relaxation, and relaxed atomistic crack-tip cases.
Added a Markov chain Monte Carlo procedure to quantify uncertainty from mesh and integration-domain choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with LEFM and VCE in all three regimes, and a silicon three-point-bending test where the critical energy release rate closely matches the Griffith criterion.
watch_item: Accuracy still depends on mesh density and the chosen integration domain, so the uncertainty model must be checked carefully for each fracture setup.
paper_title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
